population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. 16.8% of ~262M adults ≈ 44M current users, all incretin reasons. About 13M take it for type 2 diabetes and 31M for weight. Age check: 52M×9% + 86M×16% + 63M×27% + 61M×14% ≈ 4.7+13.8+17.0+8.5 = 44.0M. Cycling arithmetic: ever 23.5% − current 16.8% = 6.7% of adults have used and are off now. With ~35% one-year persistence, about 60% of ever-users (14.1% of adults) have stopped at least once. Stopped-at-least-once 14.1 − off-now 6.7 = 7.4% of adults have restarted and are on again. 7.4 ÷ 23.5 = 31% of ever-users cycled. That is ~52% eventual restart among stoppers, consistent with 36–47% within one year. The off-drug population is ~17.5M adults. Pediatric use (~1.1% of under-18s, mostly 12–17 on semaglutide) still skews to commercially insured and cash-paying households. Off-label use in 8–11-year-olds stays under specialist care. Income gap widened: bottom-third uptake rose ~4 pts, mostly via Medicaid opt-in states and gray-market generics; top-third uptake rose ~6 pts via cash pay.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot ended Dec 2027 and rolled, as pre-announced, into the voluntary CMS BALANCE Part D model on the same terms: Medicare pays ~$245/month, beneficiary copay $50. Most Part D plans participate. About 2.6M beneficiaries are covered for obesity. Medicaid covers obesity at the same $245 in roughly half of states (~2.4M enrollees); the other states cover diabetes codes only. Medicare obesity spend ≈ 2.6M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.6B/yr, which is running well above the CBO path of ≥$35B over 2026–2034 (~$4B/yr). Medicaid ≈ 2.4M × $245 × 12 ≈ $7.1B/yr, federal and state combined.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Unchanged in shape and deepening. India has 60+ brands at ~$8–48/month. Canada has generic semaglutide at ~CAD 80–110. Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generic markets, and generic semaglutide is sold in ~160 countries. Tirzepatide is still under patent almost everywhere.
access.note: FICTIONAL. The price path has stalled. Medicare's $245 became a floor rather than a waypoint. TrumpRx and manufacturer-direct cash prices are stuck at $299–349/month for maintenance doses of injectables, the Wegovy pill and Foundayo. Only oral starting doses hold at $149. Wegovy list price is still $1,349. Retatrutide launched at $1,499 list with LillyDirect cash at $749. Lilly allocates retatrutide supply through 2028, so it has no incentive to discount. After its scandal, Novo is defending margin rather than cutting price. Payer mix for the 31M weight users is: Medicare 2.6M, Medicaid 2.4M, employer plans 8.0M, brand cash-pay 13.0M, gray market 5.0M. Gray market means mail-order Indian or Canadian generics plus residual compounders. Cash outlay ≈ 13M × ~$290 × 12 ≈ $45B/yr out of pocket. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 60% to 44% (fictional Business Group on Health 2028 survey). Most remaining plans restrict cover to diabetes, established cardiovascular disease (Wegovy CV label), OSA (Zepbound) or MASH codes. FDA's proposed 503B exclusion is still being litigated by compounders. Warning letters continue. Personal importation of Indian generic semaglutide by mail is technically unlawful but rarely enforced against individuals.

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Retatrutide (BLA filed Feb 2027) was approved in Mar 2028, 13 months after filing, for BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with comorbidity. Label efficacy is 28.3% mean loss at 80 weeks, and up to ~30% at 104 weeks in BMI ≥35. That is surgical-grade loss from a pen, and the triple-agonist driver is honoured. Supply is allocated. CagriSema received an FDA Complete Response Letter in Dec 2026 citing data-integrity problems at REDEFINE trial sites. Novo plans to resubmit after re-analysis excluding the affected sites, no earlier than 2029. Compulsion indication: Foundayo's phase 3 in gambling disorder was positive (May 2028; ~40% vs 22% achieving ≥50% reduction in gambling days). Lilly filed an sNDA with priority review, with a decision expected H1 2029. The compulsion driver is therefore realised as a filing plus mainstream off-label use, not an approval. Amycretin remains in phase 3 and has not been filed. Survodutide filed in 2028 and is under review. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not on the US market. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts are still in trials.

No causal confirmation in long-term RCTs; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL litigation ongoing, no verdicts on causation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ~25–30% of lost weight is lean mass. Concern sharpened with 28%-loss retatrutide in older adults. No new data changed the estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None beyond label language; muscle-preserving adjuncts still in trials.
EMA 'very rare' label for semaglutide; no US class label.
Warning removed from US labels (Jan 2026); unchanged.

Clinicians treat it as uncommon and dose-related. The same mechanism is now the basis of an approved smoking-cessation label and a gambling filing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as an uncommon adverse reaction in the retatrutide label. No class warning. No dedicated postmarketing study required.

Further observational reports; no RCT confirmation.

safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters; 503B exclusion still in litigation; import alerts on named sellers.

food_and_beverage.state: Incretin households are ~30% of US households. Snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volumes are down low-to-mid single digits a year in those categories. Big CPG reports flat-to-negative volume and leans on price and mix. Protein, fibre and 'small-format' SKUs are standard shelf architecture. Columbus, Ohio test-market data is now cut by 'on/off' household status. Some low-income, uncovered households remain high-volume buyers of value packs, so the market is splitting by access.

alcohol.state: Volumes are contracting faster than pre-2026 trend, concentrated in spirits and high-frequency drinkers. Off-label prescribing for drinking and the smoking label make 'cut down' a mainstream medical goal. Brands push premium, low-ABV and occasion drinking; no growth category offsets the loss.

restaurants.state: Traffic is broadly flat. Average check holds through premium small plates, half portions and 'tasting' menus. Buffet and all-you-can-eat formats are closing locations. Las Vegas casino-resorts report softer late-night food and beverage spend and, anecdotally, shorter gaming sessions.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking store counts. Mainstream apparel benefits from re-sizing waves, including a new one from retatrutide users. Alterations and resale platforms grow. Some regain customers come back up the size range, which partly stabilises plus-size.

fitness.state: Strength-training and 'muscle-preservation' memberships keep growing among on-drug 50–64s. Gyms partner with telehealth prescribers. Cardio-centric chains stagnate.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 44%. Coverage is concentrated on diabetes, cardiac, OSA and MASH codes. Pharmacy trend is moderating for dropping employers and staying high for those that cover. Prior authorisation is universal. Some insurers sell standalone 'weight benefit' riders at ~$90–150/month to employees of non-covering firms.

pharma.state: Lilly is the dominant player: retatrutide, tirzepatide and Foundayo, plus the gambling filing. Novo is wounded by the CagriSema data-integrity scandal, a ~30% share-price fall from pre-scandal levels, DOJ/SEC probes and a leadership change, but still sells Wegovy injection and pill at volume. US revenue is held up by stalled prices. Ex-US revenue is eroding to generics.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among insured and affluent adults over 40, being on an incretin is unremarkable. Being off one, with a BMI that could qualify, draws a question: cost, side effects, conviction, or a regain story. A thin body no longer says 'on it' so much as 'can afford it'. A heavy body in a professional setting is increasingly read as uncovered.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The two tiers are explicit. Covered or cash-rich users get brands and, increasingly, retatrutide. Uncovered workers in non-covering firms pay $299–349 out of pocket, mail-order Indian generics, or go without. Bottom-third uptake (12.5%) trails the top (21%). In suburban Dallas–Fort Worth and Phoenix, women 45–64 are the most saturated demographic, and dropping off is what gets discussed at work.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller and shorter. Hosts plan 'half-plate' menus. Thanksgiving coverage runs 'how to host when half the table is on it' as a standard service piece. Eating large without comment is becoming a marker of youth, of being off the drug, or of a deliberate choice.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Status is disclosed casually. At least one major dating app added an optional 'GLP-1: on / off / prefer not to say' profile field in 2027. Couples' therapists report 'discordant' couples, one partner on and one off, as a recognised pattern. Libido changes are discussed as an expected trade-off, not a scandal.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite of all kinds is now a dial. The smoking label and the gambling filing make 'craving' a medical object in law and in conversation. People talk about wanting things as something they can choose to keep or turn down.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled as an uncommon adverse reaction (~1–2%) for retatrutide. Clinicians describe it as uncommon and dose-related, managed by titrating down. Patient forums claim much higher rates; no adequately powered study exists. At 44M users, even 1–2% means roughly 0.4–0.9M people with some degree of flattening.
interior_life.framing: Officially a side effect for most users, and a therapy for smokers and, pending approval, gamblers. Clinicians say 'the same quieting'. Patients use 'flat' for the bug and 'quiet' for the feature.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Occasional HR and occupational-health notes cite lowered drive after dose escalation, managed like any medication side effect. Some sales-commission and trading floors joke about 'Zepbound calm'. No systematic productivity effect is measured, and no employer encourages use for performance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Music, comedy and food writers discuss 'flat months' after titration as a recognised phase. Sports-betting apps report slightly lower handle growth in high-uptake states and attribute part of it to off-label use; this is disputed. Extreme-flavour snacks and hot sauces hold a niche with on-drug consumers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced desire is reported by a minority and accepted as a known trade-off. Some users time dose holidays around holidays or anniversaries, which adds to cycling. Discordant-couple counselling is a small but named specialty.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable effect on mood or turnout. Politics is about price: the US–India price gap and the $299–349 cash price are recurring campaign talking points in 2028, but no legislation passed.

state.regulatory_posture: Unchanged: pro-access, pro-speed approvals (retatrutide on standard review; oral semaglutide smoking label under a priority voucher) alongside continuing enforcement against compounders and illegal online sellers. No new legislation or price action.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy or mandate. Medicare $245/$50 continues via the pre-announced BALANCE Part D model. Medicaid obesity coverage depends on state opt-in. TrumpRx cash channel persists at stalled prices.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage is still conditioned on BMI or comorbidity codes and prior authorisation. Employers narrowed eligibility to diabetes and cardiac codes. There is no adherence monitoring beyond plan refill data.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The US–rest-of-world price gap widened in relative terms: US cash $299–349 vs India $8–48. Mail-order personal importation from India and Canada is a significant gray channel. Lilly's retatrutide supply is constrained by peptide manufacturing capacity, even with new US plants coming online.

open_tensions: Medicare and Medicaid obesity spend (~$15B/yr combined) is running far above CBO's score while employers exit. Public payers are becoming the main insurer of weight, and no one has voted on that.

The reward-quieting mechanism is now an approved therapy for smoking and pending for gambling, yet it is labelled a side effect for weight users. The 2029 gambling decision will force a label-level answer on whether reduced wanting is harm or benefit.
Prices have stalled in the US while generics cost $8–48 abroad. A significant mail-order gray market is supplying the uncovered bottom third, and enforcement against individuals is nil.
Novo's probes are unresolved, and nearly a third of ever-users have cycled on and off. The ~17.5M people currently off, many regaining, have no long-horizon data on what repeated cycling does.
still_true: Medicare pays ~$245/month for obesity GLP-1s with a ~$50 beneficiary copay.
There is no FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Foundayo (orforglipron) and the Wegovy pill are on the market, with oral starting doses at $149.
Suicidal ideation remains debunked and the warning stays off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels.

prose.headline: Off It? Explain Yourself. One in Six Americans Is On, the Price Won't Budge, and Your Boss Stopped Paying
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028 roughly one American adult in six takes an incretin drug: about 44 million people. Thirteen million of them take it for diabetes and the rest for weight. Among people in their fifties and early sixties the share is above a quarter. In the office parks of suburban Dallas and the cul-de-sacs east of Phoenix, nobody asks whether a colleague is on it. People ask why someone stopped. An answer is expected: the price, the nausea, the regain, a doctor, a belief. Nearly a third of everyone who has ever started has stopped and come back at least once, and about seventeen million are off right now. They are a population with its own weather. They are mostly regaining, and mostly waiting for something cheaper.

Nothing got cheaper. Medicare's $245 deal was supposed to pull the cash price down, and instead it became the floor. Manufacturer-direct and TrumpRx prices for maintenance doses have sat at $299 to $349 a month for two years. Only the oral starting doses still sell at $149. Lilly launched retatrutide in March at $1,499 list and $749 cash. It is a weekly pen that takes off about 28 percent of body weight, the kind of result that used to need surgery, and Lilly has more buyers than supply. Novo Nordisk is in no position to start a price war. In June 2027 a whistleblower complaint alleged that its executives sat on evidence of falsified data at CagriSema trial sites until the FDA rejected the drug. The chief executive left, the shares fell by about a third, and two federal probes are still open. The Wegovy injection and pill still sell in enormous volume, at the same prices.

Employers kept leaving. Fewer than half now cover the drugs for weight. Those that do mostly cover diabetes, heart disease, sleep apnea or fatty liver: a diagnosis code, not a body. The result is two tiers anyone can see. If your code qualifies or your income allows, you get the brand and maybe the new pen. If not, you pay rent-sized money each month, or you order Indian generic semaglutide by mail at a tenth of the price and hope the pen is what it says. Medicare now covers about 2.6 million people for obesity, and about half the states' Medicaid programmes cover another 2.4 million. Together that is around $15 billion a year, far beyond anything the budget office scored. The bottom income third has gained ground, but it still trails the top by eight points.

The drugs have also become official medicine for wanting less. In September the FDA approved oral semaglutide to help people with overweight quit smoking. Lilly has filed for orforglipron in gambling disorder after a trial in which twice as many people as on placebo halved their gambling days. Telehealth clinics already prescribe off-label for drinking, betting and late-night shopping. The retatrutide label lists 'affect blunting' as an uncommon reaction, one or two in a hundred. That is the same quieting the smoking label sells, called a side effect when weight patients feel it. Clinicians lower the dose. Patients distinguish 'quiet' from 'flat', and most say they are quiet.

Food companies have stopped calling this a threat and started calling it a segment. Snack and soda volumes keep slipping. Shelves are built around protein and small packs, and test-market data from Columbus is now split by whether a household is on the drug or off it. Buffets close. Las Vegas resorts report shorter nights. Distillers keep shrinking. Gyms sell muscle to fifty-five-year-olds. Dating profiles carry an on/off field. At Thanksgiving, hosts cook half as much and nobody remarks on it, except to the cousin who goes back for seconds.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Dana Ruiz sets her alarm for 5:40 so she can take the pill with four ounces of water and wait the thirty minutes before coffee. The bottle came yesterday. $299, charged to the card she keeps for things she doesn't discuss with Marco. The dental group dropped weight coverage last January. Marco's Mounjaro is still covered, because his A1c is a code and her BMI isn't anymore.

At the front desk in Mesa she checks in a woman whose chart notes 'Zepbound — CV indication' and a man who asks if they can do the cleaning before his injection kicks in Thursday. Lunch is the office's monthly order from the Mediterranean place. Six half-bowls, one full. The full one is Kayla, twenty-six. She says she's not on anything, and then explains for a while that she just isn't hungry in the mornings, as if someone had asked.

Dana's sister texts a photo of a blister pack from a site in Gujarat. Forty dollars, three months. Is this real?? Dana doesn't answer yet.

After work she walks the canal path with her neighbour Lorraine, who stopped in March. You look great, Dana says, and they both hear how it sounds.

At dinner their son Mateo, fifteen, asks whether he'd have to take it forever if he started. Marco says ask the doctor. Dana says eat your rice.

Later Marco puts on the record they danced to at their wedding and holds out his hand. She takes it. It's nice. She notices she is noticing that it's nice, and she goes to bed early.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Foundayo's phase 3 in gambling disorder was positive (May 2028; ~40% vs 22% achieving ≥50% reduction in gambling days)
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the parent world has only anecdotal and observational evidence for compulsion, and no gambling trial of any phase. A positive pivotal phase 3 within two years, plus a surge in off-label prescribing and effects on casino sessions within months, is asserted rather than shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: smoking cessation adjunct in adults with BMI ≥27 (oral semaglutide, Sep 2028)
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: nicotine evidence in the parent is anecdotal. The candidate shows no phase 3 trial or filing event, only an approval, so a full indication from an unshown pivotal program is too fast. The BMI ≥27 restriction on a smoking label also goes unexplained.

magnitude: 1.1% of all under-18s is roughly 0.8M children. The baseline had only ~0.6% of children with obesity prescribed in the 8–11 band, so this implies a jump of an order of magnitude with no stated mechanism or payer path.

rationale.badness: The world is a harder but recognisable society. Access is split into insurance, cash and gray-market tiers (top 21% vs bottom 12.5%, $299–349 cash), and ~17.5M people are off the drug and regaining with no long-horizon cycling data. Reward-quieting is labelled a side effect for weight users but sold as therapy for smokers and gamblers, and teens now ask whether they would be on it forever. The cost is largely hidden, and many gain real health benefit and obesity falls, so it is not worse than a 5.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible: +5.8pp adoption, stalled price, employer retreat at 44%, nicotine and compulsion, the triple agonist at ~28%, the Novo scandal, normalisation and niche side effect. Small strains are the quantified 'affect blunting' label entry and the smoking approval, set against safety_signal 'none', and treating the 16.8% as all-reasons use so that weight users are only ~11.8% against the 11% baseline. mechanism: The price stall (Lilly supply allocation, Novo defending margin) and the employer retreat are causally shown. The smoking approval and the positive gambling phase 3 (claims 1–2) have no trials in the parent or in the events. Retatrutide re-sizing waves and shorter gaming sessions within months of launch are asserted, and the 44% figure is dated 2027-01 in events but attributed to a 2028 survey in the note. magnitude: On-drug 16.8%, ever 23.5% (near the 23.8 edge), the income thirds, the age bands (44.0M) and the payer mix (31M) all reconcile. So do Medicare $7.6B, Medicaid $7.1B, cash $45B and the cycling arithmetic. Penalties are the 1.1% pediatric figure (claim 3), applying a 35% persistence rate to all ever-users including diabetics, and the edge-hugging ever-used figure.
rationale.generativity: The prose has strong human texture: Dana's 30-minute pill routine, the card she keeps hidden from Marco, Kayla's unprompted explanation, the Gujarat blister-pack text, Lorraine's 'you look great', and Mateo's question. The world fields add scenes: discordant couples, the dating-app field, half-plate Thanksgiving and Las Vegas shorter nights. The closing wedding-song beat shows reward flattening rather than explaining it.

least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the 2026 baseline had only ~0.6% of children with obesity prescribed, which is about 0.1% of all under-18s. A 1.1% rate across all minors is roughly a ten-fold rise in two years. The note offers no arithmetic and no mechanism, such as a new pediatric label or coverage change.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Foundayo's phase 3 in gambling disorder was positive (May 2028; ~40% vs 22% achieving ≥50% reduction in gambling days).
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the baseline has only anecdotal and observational evidence for compulsion, and no gambling trial. A phase 3 that starts, enrolls and reads out by May 2028, followed by a priority-review filing and surging off-label use, appears from nowhere. No trial-start event is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 13M take it for type 2 diabetes and 31M for weight.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the 2026 baseline of 11% on drug counted weight use only, about 28–29M adults. The candidate quietly redefines the figure as all incretin reasons. That leaves weight users at 31M, only about 2–3M above baseline, which undercuts the stipulated +5.8 pp adoption jump.

rationale.badness: This is a recognisably harder, two-tier society. Employer coverage is 44%, cash prices are stalled at $299–349, and the bottom third (12.5%) trails the top (21%). About 5M users rely on unlawful gray-market imports, and 17.5M adults are off-drug and mostly regaining. Reward blunting is labelled a side effect for weight users while it is sold as a therapy for smokers and gamblers, so people cannot easily name or measure what is happening to them. Mass harm is absent and the safety ledger is mostly unchanged, which keeps overall badness mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption is 16.8% (+5.8 pp), prices are stalled, employer coverage retreats to 44%, and retatrutide is approved at 28–30%. The Novo scandal appears as events, the nicotine indication is approved, and the compulsion driver is realised as a filing plus off-label use. Adding 'affect blunting' to the retatrutide label sits slightly awkwardly beside safety_signal 'none'. mechanism: The scandal, price stall and employer retreat chains are shown. Two things are asserted rather than shown: the nicotine approval and gambling phase 3 results appear with no trial or readout events (claim 2), and the pediatric prevalence jump has no cause (claim 1). The redefinition of 'on drug' to include diabetes is also unexplained (claim 3). The prose chart note 'Zepbound — CV indication' conflicts with the world, which gives the CV label to Wegovy. magnitude: On drug (16.8%) and ever-used (23.5%, near the 23.8 edge) are inside the envelope. The income thirds average to the national figure, and the age bands sum to 44M. Payer mix sums to 31M. Medicare ($7.6B), Medicaid ($7.1B) and cash ($45B) all multiply out, and the cycling arithmetic reconciles. Retatrutide timing (filed Feb 2027, approved 13 months later) respects the approval rules. Deductions are for the pediatric 1.1% and for the weight-versus-all-reasons definition shift.
rationale.generativity: The day in the life is rich: Dana's 5:40 pill routine, the hidden card, the Gujarat blister-pack text, Kayla's unprompted explanation, Lorraine's 'you look great', and Mateo asking whether he'd take it forever. The final dance scene shows reward blunting rather than explaining it. The world fields add texture: the dating-app on/off field, discordant couples, half-plate Thanksgiving and Las Vegas shorter nights. Many scenes are implied.
